depth_findings.text: The local time in the date notice changes every minute and sits before the history under the legacy prompt order, so provider prefix caching misses on every turn once the switch is on; the owner must choose the precision (minute, hour or date only) before the switch goes on.

Do runs get the notice only when the run-context mode is on, and the proto grep finds no date field in RunContext or RunAgentRequest, so the design's claim that WS02-S6 carries the date is unsupported; whether Do runs need a dated field (a proto change) is an owner call.
No unit test checks the ZDR system message with a notice present, and the design's named ZDR golden s_local_time_allowed_under_zdr (mp-contracts zdr posture matrix) is not added.
Nothing tests that json_handlers.rs and ag_ui.rs forward the three fields; a missed lead line would silently drop the clock and the language on JSON and AG-UI turns.
The design says the calendar slot uses the local date as today, but calendar_context.rs has no notion of today, so that sentence has no code path and the calendar is unchanged.

Two language vocabularies now reach model-gateway on one request: ui_locale (no or en, this slice) and the WS16-S6 locale (nb-NO or en-US); locale_hint::hint_sentence is not called yet, so wiring it later would state the language twice.
The Pacific/Auckland live proof and the rendered-notice log from the model-gateway debug output are not run; this is a depth-phase lead step.
On a ZDR turn the local time becomes new prompt content once the switch is on; the design's ZDR clause allows it with no store, and the ZDR live proof should confirm it.
The zone-name shape check now exists in the BFF shared.rs and in model-gateway locale_context.rs; a shared list of accepted and refused names in both test suites would keep them aligned.
The SPA sends the zone, the offset and the stored language on every turn even with the switch off, a wire change the design approved; the gateway ignores them until the switch is on.

The date clause carries the local time to the minute, so with the switch on the date notice changes every minute; under the legacy prompt order it sits before the history and breaks provider prefix caching on every turn, so the precision must be decided before the switch goes on.

Do runs get the local notice only through the run-context composition (RunContextMode not Off); with run context off, Do runs carry no local date, and no proto field carries a date into RunAgentRequest. The owner must decide whether a dated field is needed.

No test checks zdr_turn_settings_with with Some(local_notice) (every existing call passes None), and the design's ZDR golden s_local_time_allowed_under_zdr in mp-contracts zdr_posture_matrix is not added.

No BFF test confirms that json_handlers.rs and ag_ui.rs call with_locale_context. Until the lead lines land, those paths forward the three raw fields unvalidated. model-gateway checks them again, so this is safe, but the BFF validation is bypassed there.
The design's sentence that calendar_context::reference_calendar uses the local date as today has no code path: calendar_context.rs is unchanged, so calendar resolution stays UTC-based.
Two language vocabularies reach model-gateway on one request: ui_locale (no/en, this slice) and the WS16-S6 locale (nb-NO/en-US). If locale_hint is ever wired as well, the language is stated twice.

A send settles as failed when neither a connected nor a done frame arrives (sendContent finally). A connection lost after the gateway accepted the turn therefore restores its text, and a resend mints a new client message id, so the gateway stores a second turn.

A reload between send start and the connected frame restores the sent text from sessionStorage into the composer, because the draft is kept until the send settles. The transcript may already show that turn, so the person could send it twice.

On a thread switch, rebind() replaces the composer with the next thread's draft even when the text being left was not stored (a refused write, storage full), so that text is lost. No test covers a refused write during a switch.

Deleting the active thread (the removal path in use-chat-controller.ts that calls resetChatState) and clearing history leave that thread's draft in sessionStorage until sign-out or the 30-thread cap evicts it. The draft key should be removed with the thread.

Drafts are written for every thread origin, including Space, Support and project threads. The composer is disabled on foreign-origin threads, but the row does not say whether their drafts may be stored. Owner to decide.

A regenerate or edit-resubmit clears the composer as before. On acceptance its draft is discarded, as before, and a failure now gives the text back. Confirm that is the intended meaning of discard-on-accepted for those turns.

The controller wiring test covers an onError failure and the connected and done acceptance. Not covered: a rejected streamChat, transport loss before connected, Stop before connected, and New chat while a send is in flight.

accepted, failed and beginSend read the composer with untrack(message). Solid 2 applies signal writes at the next flush, so a caller that settles a send in the same synchronous run as a setInput would read the old text. The controller calls them in separate runs today; keep it that way.

results.notes: EP-3-S1 is built in wave mode with no flag, proto or migration. Chat drafts live in sessionStorage under verevon.chat-draft.v1:<org>:<user>:<thread|new>, with an index that keeps the 30 most recently written thread drafts. useChatThreadDraft (new, chat-thread-draft.ts) follows the Home draft gate: Temporary chat, workspace ZDR and tainted text never write, and turning either on removes the stored draft. A send clears the composer but keeps its text stored until the send settles: connected or done discards it, and a send that ends without either gives the text back to the composer if it is still that thread's composer. New chat keeps the old thread's draft. A new chat's draft moves to the thread id the conversation takes. Sign-out and identity change clear chat drafts beside the Home drafts, and the ZDR workspace clear (clearHomeLocalContent) does too. Home's key and functions are unchanged: home-draft-storage.ts has no removed lines. Other slices' uncommitted changes are present in this worktree and were not touched.
